subject: Plotting ECDFs the same way plot(ecdf(...)) does it

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Plotting ECDFs the same way plot(ecdf(...)) does it
parts:
Presently ggplot2 doesn't have any built-in logic for plotting
empirical CDFs. The appropriate geom (geom_step) does exist, but
you've got to do the statistical reduction yourself, which is a little
fiddly. More seriously, I can't find a good way to extend the
staircase to the left and right of the distribution, the way
plot.stepfun() does in base graphics. For individual plots, I can
manually add points beyond the actual distribution as part of the
statistical reduction, and then use coord_cartesian to chop off the
graph at the left and right so it *looks* like the staircase goes all
the way to the edges; but this is awkward and doesn't work with
faceting.

(Attached are two screenshots of ECDFs from the same distribution -
one is what base graphics does, the other is the best approximation to
the same I've managed with ggplot2 and without manual coord_cartesian
limit adjustment; code to reproduce both is appended. Note that I
don't insist on the dotted lines at y=0 and y=1.)

Can anyone suggest a better approach?

zw

ct <- c(2.32229, 5.01807, 5.32387, 5.69742, 6.39509, 6.9729,
13.4403, 23.302, 23.3081, 34.9627, 37.3886, 41.102)
plot(ecdf(ct), verticals=TRUE, do.points=FALSE, main=NA)

ct2 <- structure(list(
x = c(0, 2.32229, 5.01807, 5.32387, 5.69742, 6.39509,
6.9729, 13.4403, 23.302, 23.3081, 34.9627, 37.3886, 41.102,
44.2044), y = c(0, 0.0833333, 0.166667, 0.25, 0.333333, 0.416667,
0.5, 0.583333, 0.666667, 0.75, 0.833333, 0.916667, 1, 1)),
.Names = c("x", "y"), row.names=1:14, class = "data.frame")

ggplot(ct2, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_step() + ylab("Fn(x)")

That's a neat trick -- I didn't know you could do that with aes() --
but it doesn't work any better with faceting than my coord_cartesian
approach did (the problem is fundamentally one of having to manually
set scale or coord limits, which you cannot do when faceting unless
all the plots should have the same axis limits).

zw

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Re: Plotting ECDFs the same way plot(ecdf(...)) does it
parts:
On Mon, Jun 27, 2011 at 2:19 PM, Marius Hofert
<marius...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> That's nice, I was looking for something similar, including points.
> Maybe an expert knows how to nicely remove the first and last point
> drawn by geom_point() (since those points do not correspond to actual
> observations / values in ct)
It seems like this ought to work but it doesn't:

ggplot(NULL) + layer(geom="step", aes(x=c(0, ct, 45), y=c(0,
ecdf(ct)(ct), 1))) +
layer(geom="point", aes(x=ct, y=ecdf(ct)(ct)))

--> Error: When _setting_ aesthetics, they may only take one value.
Problems: x,y

This worked for me but there's probably a more elegant way to do it:

d1 = data.frame(x=c(0, ct, 45), y=c(0, ecdf(ct)(ct), 1))
d2 = data.frame(x=ct, y=ecdf(ct)(ct))
ggplot(NULL, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_step(data=d1) + geom_point(data=d2)

zw
